Alex.confusing: How the hug interacted with visiting: my Owl was hugged in round 3 and I couldn't tell whether Drew was a Floofer or a Floofer had visited me. Casey was the Floofer who visited me, and I accused the wrong player.
Alex.fun: Round 1, when I caught Ellis lying about being the Eagle. I used my real Eagle result, and a 36-point throw banked.
Alex.change: Give dead players a small way to keep helping, or soften the Wink so one early kill doesn't remove the player who holds key information.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I told the table I was hugged and named Drew as the likely Floofer, then threw 2 cards at Drew. A Floofer who visited me was just as likely, so I should have laid out both possibilities without pointing at Drew. I should also have thrown fewer cards, since I was unsure.

Blair.confusing: Dawn reports were hard to trust, since confusion and hugs meant a player's claimed visit could be wrong even when they were honest. I also couldn't tell whether Owl and Turkey claims were consistent with egg counts.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when I was the Floofer, Finley and Casey both claimed my Falcon visit showed a Turkey or Owl story that didn't add up, and I had to talk my way out of being eggsecuted while the table split.
Blair.change: I'd clarify up front what a Floofer hug does to the visitor's dawn report, because hugged players were treated as liars in the day discussion.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I used my Wink on Alex, a Farm player, and then pushed the vote onto Drew, a Farm player; I should have winked Ellis, the Eagle who was pressing me, and kept Alex alive as a Farm ally.

Casey.confusing: Who could be confused: I assumed only a visited Kookaburra causes it, and the Meowfia stake rule (2x only if the eggsecuted Farm player is the target) was easy to misread. The 'Grudge' doubling in the final result wasn't in the rules text I saw.
Casey.fun: Round 2: working out that Blair was the Floofer by matching my hug with Finley's hugged visit, and then the whole table piling onto her.
Casey.change: I'd make the stake and scoring rules clearer, including the Grudge doubling, and I'd show a Wink kill's timing or consequences so dead-player reasoning is less guessy.
Casey.regret: None that matter. In round 1 I pushed Ellis confidently without knowing, though it worked out, and in round 3 I briefly aimed at Finley before joining the Drew vote. Going straight onto the table's consensus target would have been cleaner.

Drew.confusing: The Confused rule was hard to use: my Round 1 report said I was confused, which made my own Kookaburra visit to Alex unreliable, and I never found a clean way to check it. The score bonus from banked cards versus kept cards was also unclear until the end.
Drew.fun: Round 1 went well: I threw at Ellis with the table's help, Farm won, and my banked 2 cards were worth 4 points. Watching Alex's Eagle and Owl claims clash was also entertaining.
Drew.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about who the confused player is, so the table can tell real claims from bad ones.
Drew.regret: In Round 3 I threw my high cards at Blair, when Blair was Meowfia, but I was still eggsecuted as Farm; I should have kept my 9s and 12 and thrown only low cards and Wilds to limit the loss.

Ellis.confusing: How Hug and Floofer interact with visitor reports. In round 3 I couldn't tell whether Alex's "hugged" report meant Drew was the Floofer or that someone else had visited Alex.
Ellis.fun: Round 2: my honest Eagle read on Finley, plus the Floofer clue chain, got Blair eggsecuted with a 28-point stake banked.
Ellis.change: Make the Meowfia 2x bonus and the 5-point round bonus less swingable. Casey's 132 came mostly from one huge banking, which decided the game.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw three high cards (22 points) at Drew, who was Farm. I'd have kept my best cards and thrown only low ones. Alex's hug claim, and the wink right after it, fit a Floofer cat like Casey silencing him, so I was too sure about Drew.

Finley.confusing: The throw rules were the hardest to track: how banked versus discarded cards work, and how a return to the nest depends on whether your target was on the other team. Knowing who was Meowfia also got harder when Alex's and Drew's claims were unverifiable after they died.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when my Owl visit to Blair got me hugged and that exposed Blair as the Floofer. The table converged on the right cat and Farm banked a big win.
Finley.change: I would make death and Wink information clearer, since a dead player's claims can't be checked and that decided round 3. I would also let players see each other's throw values after eggsecution so bluffing is less one-sided.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I voted with the table to eggsecute Drew, a Farm player, on the strength of Alex's dead hug story. I should have pushed harder on Casey's shifting votes and questioned the Ellis-Blair pairing before joining the rush.
